connector: Today the fight is settled. But the part that carries the theme isn’t who wins. It’s how the winning happens. Watch for one moment in the duel that could easily have gone the other way, and ask what that small choice proves.

a.raw: trumpkin danced with delight and shouted the high king up old narnia
a.fixed: Trumpkin danced with delight and shouted, “The High King! Up, Old Narnia!”
a.why: Capital T on Trumpkin; no comma after delight (danced and shouted share one subject); a comma after shouted before the quote; capitals and exclamation points inside the quotation marks.

b.raw: edmund bit his lips till the blood came as the sword flashed down on peter
b.fixed: Edmund bit his lips till the blood came, as the sword flashed down on Peter.
b.why: Lewis’s own sentence. Capitals on Edmund and Peter; a comma before as, which adds what was happening at that moment; a period ends it.

notes.wgrd: Watch how the fight is settled, not just who wins. Find the moment it could have gone otherwise, and name the idea it proves.
vocab: An invitation to fight or compete that must be answered.
Fighting; single combat is one against one.
To say words aloud for someone else to write down.
An official who oversees a contest and keeps order.
notes.wordParts: Review of the unit’s bases: port, tract, struct, spect, ject, script/scribe, rupt, duct/duce, form, plus press = push, tain = hold, lev = lift.
notes.grammar: Dialogue punctuation: quotation marks fence off the exact words; the comma or end mark goes inside the closing quotation mark; a tag like said Peter joins with a comma. Lewis lets a speaker shout in fragments when the action is fast.
notes.spelling: Cumulative review: a hard word is often two or three rules stacked up. Take it apart: se + par + ate + ion; forget + t + able.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: In Chapter 14 the duel is fought and Narnia wakes. Read each moment. Tap the pillar it shows best.

items.t: During a rest, Peter says quietly, “Give my love to — to everyone at home, Ed, if he gets me.” Then he goes back into the lists.
items.why: He knows he might die and goes back anyway.
items.hint: What does Peter think might happen?

items.t: Miraz trips on a tussock and falls face down. Peter steps back and waits for him to rise.
items.why: He won’t strike an enemy who has fallen by accident.

items.t: Peter’s wrist is hurt. Edmund and Doctor Cornelius bind it up tight so he can keep fighting.
items.hint: What do they do for Peter?

items.t: Aslan finds a little old woman dying in her bed. She opens her eyes and says, “Oh, Aslan! I knew it was true. I’ve been waiting for this all my life.”
items.why: She kept believing her whole life, when no one around her did.

transcripts.welcome: Hello again, it’s Nell. Today the duel is fought. Today’s question: what matters more, who wins, or how?
transcripts.read: Read the duel slowly, through Edmund’s eyes. Find the moment when Peter could have done the easy thing, and didn’t. Then follow Aslan, Lucy and Susan through the countryside, where a whole country is waking up.
transcripts.grammar: Dialogue. Quotation marks go around the exact words. The comma or the end mark goes inside the closing quotation mark. Then the tag: said Trumpkin, cried Edmund. A fast shout can be just a fragment. The marks around it still follow the rules.
